3. Update `docs/v3/VISUAL-DESIGN.md`: mark the in-scope §9 rows decided with a link to `DESIGN.md`, and tighten any §3–§7 text the design contradicts in the same change (§10).
4. **Ask for ratification.** Put every open question to the owner and revise until `## Open questions` reads `None.`; then ask whether to ratify. Without an explicit go-ahead, **park**: set `status: blocked`, run `pnpm backlog:build`, and commit the prepared work (the grader, the exports, `DESIGN.md`, the VISUAL-DESIGN edits) — that checkpoint commit satisfies rule 6, so other stories may run meanwhile (rule 18). Then stop. A later session sets `status: doing` to revise or to ratify.
5. **Ratify — only on the owner's explicit go-ahead.** Write `docs/v3/visual/standings-search-settings/RATIFIED.md`: `Ratified by:` (the owner), `Date:` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `Source version:` (verbatim from `DESIGN.md`'s `## Source`), `Go-ahead:` (the owner's words, quoted verbatim), and a `## Manifest` with one `<sha256>  <file>` line per other file in the directory. Then set `status: done`, run `pnpm backlog:build`, run `scripts/verify-S34.sh`, `scripts/audit.sh story S34`, add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry, commit. From then on the manifest's files are sealed: a change is a ratified amendment (rule 18), never an edit.

Every export in `docs/v3/visual/standings-search-settings/` — every file other than `DESIGN.md`, `RATIFIED.md`, `REVISIONS.md` (S35–S38's revision log), and anything under `amendments/` — is named `<screen>[-<state>]-<mobile|medium|desktop>.<png|svg|pdf>` in lowercase `[a-z0-9]` words joined by `-` (the optional `<state>` may be several kebab words). For each screen — `standings`, `search`, `settings` — a file matches `^<screen>(-[a-z0-9]+)*-mobile\.(png|svg|pdf)$` and a file matches `^<screen>(-[a-z0-9]+)*-(medium|desktop)\.(png|svg|pdf)$`. **Gap:** S32 and S33 ratified the game view's chrome on 2026-10-14: a `game-topbar` (← back to that day's scoreboard · `AWY @ HOM` · live indicator only while in progress · date) with **no score and no team/score header module**, scrollable top tabs whose set follows the game's phase (pre-game: Videos · Plays · Box; in progress: + Live; final: + Recap, never Live and Recap together), and one shared loading / empty / error example for every room. At HEAD `web/src/pages/GamePage.tsx` does the opposite: it renders the score as a `Title` above the tabs, a venue line and a status badge in the header, and all five tabs for every game. Both DESIGN.md "Work required" sections assign this chrome to "S2 / S3 / S10 / S19", but none of those stories' ACs require it, so each would build its room under the wrong header — or all four would fight over `GamePage.tsx`. ### S3 — Live tab status block — score, count, outs, inning

**Gap:** Live tab is incomplete: inning / inning state / outs render; balls and strikes do not; no component test.

**Impact:** Before S3, the Live tab showed the inning and outs but not the ball-strike count or the score — no way to tell 0-2 from 3-0. S3 impact: a game in progress opens its Live tab on a compact status block with the score, the count as ball / strike / out pips, and the inning — the details a fan actually watches a live at-bat for.

**Re-scoped by the 2026-10-19 design intake review:** the inning label becomes a `packages/domain` function the scoreboard reuses, and the tablet / desktop status card is asserted (ADR-025, ratified `live-medium` / `live-desktop`).

At HEAD the Plays tab is the pre-design baseline: `web/src/components/pitch/PlaysPanel.tsx` renders every at-bat of the game as one flat accordion with the first one open. ### S128 — Standings follow the season — the final table in the off-season, spring training's in the spring

**Gap:** `GET /api/v1/standings` asks MLB for the standings on one date (`standingsUrl`, `functions/src/adapters/http/mlb.ts`). MLB has none for any date after the regular season or before it (spring training, the postseason and the off-season all answer 0 records, checked 2026-11-07), so from the last regular-season day until the next opening day the Standings page says "No standings for this date." The owner wants the final table there (owner, 2026-11-07: *"Yes, it should always show the last standings for the prior season until spring training’s first game"*), and spring training's own standings from the first spring game until opening day (owner, 2026-11-07, asked what to show then, with spring training standings suggested: *"Agreed"*).

**Impact:** Before S128, Standings was empty for half the year. S128 impact: after the regular season ends, Standings shows how the season finished until spring training starts, and during spring training it shows the spring standings.

Before every known season, or with no calendar, it is the regular-season shape for the day itself. `SeasonCalendar` gains `regularSeasonStartDate` and `regularSeasonEndDate` (MLB's season dates carry both); a calendar missing either keeps working for the scoreboard's default day (S111 unchanged) and counts as unknown here. Tested at each boundary on the committed `seasons-2025.json` / `seasons-2026.json` and a 2027 calendar: the last regular-season day and the day after, a postseason day, a January day (the previous season's final table), the day before `springStartDate` and that day, the day before `regularSeasonStartDate` and that day, a day after an early opener while other teams still play spring games (2025-03-20, after the Tokyo Series opened 2025 on 03-18: regular season, by this rule), and a final table kept while the next season's calendar isn't published.

Each shape is one `MlbStatsClient` method with its URL built by one named function as `standingsUrl` is, and the recorder records the same URLs. ### S139 — Standings serves three views and says which one opens

**Gap:** The owner wants Standings to show three views (owner, 2026-11-10: *"I think the standings view should have an option. Basically, it should be capable of showing spring training, regular season, and playoffs."*), with rules for which can be chosen on a day and which opens first (FEATURES, Standings row). `GET /api/v1/standings` serves one table per day, the one `standingsPhase` picks (S128; `packages/domain/src/standings-phase.ts`, `functions/src/services/standings.ts`). Nothing says which views a day offers or which opens first, and a fan can't ask for a view: in spring training there is no way to see the regular season's table, and in the playoffs none to see the teams that made it.

**Impact:** Before S139, the standings data was one table chosen by the calendar. S139 impact: the data can answer for spring training, the regular season or the playoffs on any day, and says which of them a fan can choose that day and which opens first, so S130's page can offer the choice. Nothing on the page changes yet.

**Source:** Feature: Standings

**Depends on:** **S128** (the table per phase and the season calendars this builds on).

**Scope files:** `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/domain/`, `packages/ports/`, `openapi/`, `fixtures/`, `web/src/api/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `docs/v3/audit.jsonl`, `docs/v3/INDEX.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S139.sh` performs)

1. One named, tested function in `packages/domain` (ADR-025), beside `standingsPhase`, answers for a day, the season calendars it is given, and whether any team in that day's regular-season table has clinched a playoff spot: the views a fan can choose that day, in the order `spring`, `regularSeason`, `playoffs`, and the one that opens first. It reads the day and the calendars only, never the clock, so a past date gets the answer it would have had on that day (owner, 2026-11-10: *"Same rules as if that date were today."*). The rules, from the owner's words of 2026-11-10 quoted in FEATURES' Standings row except where marked as the agent's:
    - **`regularSeason`** can always be chosen. It opens first on every day the two rules below don't name.
    - **`spring`** can be chosen from a season's `springStartDate` through April 15 of that season's year (owner: *"In fact, just do April 15th."*), or through the day before its `regularSeasonStartDate` when that is later (the agent's choice for a season that opens after April 15, as 2020's did; the owner's rule names April 15 only). It opens first from `springStartDate` through the day before `regularSeasonStartDate`.
    - **`playoffs`** can be chosen on a day from a season's `regularSeasonStartDate` through the day before the next known season's `springStartDate` (with no later season known, with no end), when a team has clinched. That end is the agent's reading, for the owner to accept or change: the owner's words keep the view after the Series (*"I think we should keep the playoffs view showing."*) and say nothing of when it goes. It opens first from the day after `regularSeasonEndDate` through the sixth day after that season's `lastGameDate`, when it can be chosen; from the seventh day the regular season opens first again and `playoffs` can still be chosen (owner: *"A week after the last playoff game, we should switch back to the regular season by default"*).
    - Before every known season, or with no calendar, only `regularSeason`.

    Unit tests with the 2026 and 2027 calendars, each day with and without a clinched team where that changes the answer: 2027-02-18 (the off-season's last day), 2027-02-19 (spring opens first; `playoffs` gone), 2027-03-24, 2027-03-25 (the regular season opens first; `spring` still offered), 2027-04-15 and 2027-04-16 (`spring` offered, then not), 2026-09-05, 2026-09-27 (the regular season's last day: it still opens first), 2026-09-28 (`playoffs` opens first; with no clinched team the regular season does), the sixth and seventh days after 2026's `lastGameDate`, a season whose first regular-season game is after April 15, and no calendar.

2. `GET /api/v1/standings` takes `view` beside `date`, and its answer gains `view` (the view the returned table belongs to) and `views: { offered, default }` from AC 1's function. `phase`, `season` and `date` keep S128's meaning and describe the table returned; `phase`'s values don't change.
    - **No `view`:** the answer is the table S128 serves today, unchanged, plus the new fields (`view` is `spring` for a spring table, otherwise `regularSeason`). A client that doesn't know views (the page before S130, an installed app that hasn't updated) keeps getting a full table.
    - **`view=default`:** the day's default view. On the first spring day that is spring's table, even while it has no team yet, with `view: "spring"`; the day before it is last season's final table (owner, 2026-11-10: *"spring training standings should show on that day. The day before should show the prior season's standings."*). On opening day's morning it keeps S128 AC 3's fallback: spring's last table while the regular season's is empty, and `view` names that table's view.
    - **`view=spring`, `regularSeason` or `playoffs`:** that view when the day offers it; when it doesn't, the answer `view=default` gives, so an old or shared link still shows standings and the answer's `view` says which.
    - **Anything else:** 400 `view_invalid`, with a hint naming the four values.

    The tables: `spring` is that spring's table as of the day, or as of the day before `regularSeasonStartDate` once the regular season has started. `regularSeason` is the day's table in a regular season, the season's final table from its end until the next `springStartDate` (S128's `final`), and on a spring day the new season's regular-season table for that day (`phase: "regularSeason"`), except on a spring day whose spring table has no team yet (AC 3's last rule). `playoffs` is the `regularSeason` view's table for that day keeping only the teams with `clinched`, in the same division order, a division with none left out (the page shows them with no numbers, owner: *"it'll just be a list of teams with no with no numbers"*) (route tests on recorded fixtures: every case above, `?date=2026-10-05` with each of the four values, and `?date=2027-02-19`, a first spring morning, since the fixtures hold no 2027 spring table, with each of the four values).

3. The regular season before its first game. When `view=regularSeason` is asked for by name and MLB's regular-season table for that season has no team (a spring day, or opening day's morning), the answer lists that spring's teams in their divisions, in name order, each with 0 wins and 0 losses, `clinched` and `divisionLeader` false and every other figure `null` (the agent's proposal for the owner's *"even though like in spring training, it's going to be all, you know, blank for the regular season, we should still show it"*, for the owner to accept or change; S129 draws how blank looks). On a spring day whose spring table has no team yet (the first spring morning), there are no teams to list, so `view=regularSeason` answers last season's final table, with `view: "regularSeason"` (the 2026-11-10 backlog review's proposal, for the owner to accept or change when S129 is ratified; see the note). ### S140 — Standings names the World Series winner

**Gap:** Once the World Series is over, the owner wants Standings to say who won it, in a celebratory box above the regular season's table (owner, 2026-11-10: *"A week after the last playoff game, we should switch back to the regular season by default for the standings, but with a box above that says like blank team won the World Series, view the playoffs standings page or whatever"*). Nothing BT serves names the winner: the standings answer holds the regular season's records, and the World Series schedule is read only for the season's last game day (`mapSeasonCalendar`, `functions/src/mappers/season-calendar.ts`).

**Impact:** Before S140, BT's data never said who won the World Series. S140 impact: in the off-season the standings data names the champion, so S130's page can show the owner's celebratory box. Nothing on the page changes yet.

One named, tested function decides it: the winner is the team whose series wins, in the season's last final World Series game that wasn't cancelled, are more than half of that game's `gamesInSeries` (4 of 7; 5 of 9 in 1903 and 1919–1921). It answers no winner while the series is under way, for a season with no World Series (1901, 1902, 1904, 1994), for an empty schedule, and when the payload lacks `gamesInSeries` or the teams' series records: never a guess (tests on `fixtures/raw/worldseries-2025.json`: the Dodgers, in seven games; `worldseries-2026.json`: the Brewers, in five; `worldseries-2027.json`, which is empty: none; the 2026 recording cut to its first four games: none; a payload with neither field: none).

The off-season starts the day after the regular season ends, while the playoffs are still being played, and MLB's schedule for a past season already holds the deciding game, so a day before it names no champion: a past date gets the answer it would have had on that day (as S139 AC 1 says of the views). `wonOn` is the day of the game that decided the Series, the game AC 1 reads the winner from, so the page can count days from it (S130 AC 4). ### S130 — Standings shows its spring training, regular season and playoffs views

**Gap:** The owner wants Standings to show spring training, the regular season or the playoffs, with the fan able to switch (owner, 2026-11-10: *"I think the standings view should have an option. Basically, it should be capable of showing spring training, regular season, and playoffs."*), to say which day's standings these are when it isn't today, to celebrate the World Series winner in the off-season, and to title the page by what is shown (FEATURES, Standings row). The page (`web/src/pages/StandingsPage.tsx`) draws the one table it is given under the heading "Standings", spring training's like the regular season's. S139 and S140 put the views and the winner in the data; nothing shows them.

**Impact:** Before S130, Standings showed one table and spring training's looked like the real thing. S130 impact: a fan can switch between spring training, the regular season and the playoffs when each applies, the page opens on the one that matters that day, says "Standings as of" a past day, and celebrates the World Series winner in the off-season.

1. **The switch.** The page asks for standings through `useStandings` with `view=default` when its address names no view, and with the address's `?view=` when it names one. It draws S129's switch from the answer: the views in `views.offered`, the answer's `view` marked. Choosing a view puts it in the address beside any `?date=`, which is kept, so the view can be linked and Back returns to the one before. When the address names a view other than `default` and the answer's `view` isn't that one (that day doesn't offer it), the page shows what came back and corrects the address without adding a history entry. An address that names no view, or `view=default`, is never corrected: it asks `view=default` on every visit, so the day's default opens, whatever view came back. The corrected address asks under a new cache key, so the table that came back stays on screen while it is asked for again: no loading state shows between the two. An answer with no `views` (cached from before S139) draws the table as today with no switch (RTL: each set of offered views S129 draws; choosing one; an address asking for a view not offered, asserting the table never leaves the screen and the loading state never shows after the first answer; an address with no `?view=`, and one with `?view=default`, each answered with a `view` that isn't `views.default`, asserting the address is unchanged; an answer without `views`).
2. **Each view.** Spring training's tables have no games-behind column; the regular season's keep it. The regular season before its first game and the playoffs list are drawn as S129 draws them, the playoffs list with no numbers. With no day in the address, or today's, there is no line. The date is formatted by one named function in `web/src/format/datetime.ts` (RTL: a past day in each view; today's date in the address; no date).
4. **The World Series box.** When the answer has a `champion` and S129's rule for when the box shows is met, the page draws S129's box above the table: the winner's name and a link to the playoffs view that keeps the address's `?date=`. ### S9 — Representative local dev: `pnpm dev` on the Firestore emulator

**Superseded 2026-10-18** (never started) by [ADR-017](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-017--platform-cloudflare-workers--neon-postgres-accepted-2026-10-18): the Firestore emulator workflow it set up is gone. Its storage-contract cases moved to **S46**, its representative-local-dev requirement to **S51**.

**Gap:** Production is meant to store schedules and games in Firestore through the S7 adapter, but nothing has ever run that adapter against Firestore. The repo has no Firebase CLI, no script starts the emulator, this machine has no Java runtime (checked 2026-10-09), and S7's emulator round-trip is skipped in every run. `pnpm dev` uses the in-memory repositories, which behave differently from Firestore: they hand back the very object they stored, while Firestore returns a JSON-plain copy. A feature can therefore pass every local check and fail once deployed. `local-server.ts` runs `main()` on import, so the composition `pnpm dev` actually runs has no test. ADR-013 already says `pnpm dev` runs on the emulators; the code never did.

**Impact:** Before S9, local development "worked", but on storage that behaves differently from production. Nothing proved that a feature working on a laptop would also work deployed. S9 impact: `pnpm dev` runs the app against Google's local copy of the real database, with no cloud account and nothing deployed, so working locally becomes a reliable sign of working in production.

**Source:** Pillar: Delightful — for developers too: local development works without serious setup or a deployed cloud environment, and is representative enough that a feature that works locally very likely works deployed. Approved by owner 2026-10-09: "Delightful. It applies to developers as well, and a local development experience that requires serious setup is a pain in the ass."

**Owner's requirements (2026-10-09, verbatim):** local development *"works, doesn't require its own serverless architecture that has to be deployed just for testing, and … is representative in such a way that a feature which works locally is very likely to work after being deployed"*. *"pnpm dev should be the canonical development path for running locally. If emulators are important for that, it should use emulators."* Then, having weighed a separate in-memory dev command: *"ditch the in-memory one and go emulator-only."* The owner also confirmed the Delightful approval covers this re-scope, and that CI does **not** run the emulator.

**Approach (one path):**

- **`pnpm dev` is the only way to run the app locally.** It starts the Firestore emulator under a `demo-` project ID (no real Firebase project, no login, nothing deployed), seeds it from `fixtures/` on startup, and runs the API and web against it. Data starts fresh each run. The one prerequisite is a Java runtime, which the emulator needs.
- **There is no in-memory way to run the app.** The in-memory repositories stay only as **test doubles** for the fast `functions` tests (CI has no emulator), and they are held to the same **storage contract** as the Firestore adapters so they can't drift from Firestore's behavior.
- **Projections and replay records stay in memory even under `pnpm dev`**, because no Firestore adapter exists for them yet (the *store-to-port promotion* Later theme). The README says so.

**Depends on:** S7 (Firestore adapters — `done`)

**Scope files:** `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `firebase.json`, `firestore.indexes.json`, `functions/src/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S9.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).
1. Write the storage contract (AC 1) and run it against the in-memory test doubles (AC 2). Where they differ from Firestore, change the doubles (store and return copies), not the contract. If a service turns out to rely on the old aliasing, that is a real production bug this story exists to find: fix it in `functions/src/`.
2. Run the same contract against the Firestore adapters behind the emulator guard (AC 3). Clear emulator state between cases with the emulator's `DELETE /emulator/v1/projects/<id>/databases/(default)/documents` endpoint on `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`, and take the project ID from `GCLOUD_PROJECT` (which `firebase emulators:exec` sets) rather than a hard-coded one.
3. Split `local-server.ts` into a testable `createLocalServer` that takes its repositories, and an entrypoint that always uses Firestore (AC 4). Remove the `BT_USE_FIRESTORE` switch.
4. Add `firebase-tools`, the `dev` and `test:emulated` scripts, and the index file (AC 5–6); document local development (AC 7–8).
5. Set `status: done`, run `pnpm backlog:build`, update the Current baseline (the "Firestore" and "Emulator-based `pnpm dev`" rows), run `scripts/audit.sh story S9`, add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry, commit.

1. `functions/src/adapters/repository-contract.ts` exists and exports `describeSnapshotRepositoryContract`. The function takes a label and a factory returning `{ schedules: ScheduleRepository; games: GameRepository }` over empty storage. It seeds from the committed fixtures through `FixtureMlbStatsClient`: the file names `FixtureMlbStatsClient`, `2024-07-04`, and `744834`, so the real game with its plays is stored, not a toy object. It declares at least five `it(` cases, covering:
   - (a) a read after upsert deep-equals `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(written))`, the shape Firestore returns;

### S46 — Repository ports + shared storage contract + versioned snapshots

**Gap:** ADR-018: access only through repository ports — including the projection and replay stores — and one shared repository test suite run against every adapter; ADR-022: every update carries a monotonic `version`. At HEAD `GameProjectionRepository` (`functions/src/services/projection-store.ts`) and the replay-artifact repository (`replay-store.ts`) are declared in `functions/`, not `packages/ports`; the in-memory repositories hand back the stored object itself (the aliasing S9 found); and `GameSnapshot` / `ScheduleDay` carry `fetchedAt` but no `version` or `lastChangedAt`. Carries S9's contract cases (a)–(e) now that S9 is superseded. Inserted by the 2026-10-18 backlog review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S46, the in-memory stores behaved differently from a real database, and nothing could tell a new game update from a stale one. S46 impact: every store is held to one shared set of behaviors, and every game and schedule carries a version so a late or repeated update can never overwrite a newer one.

**Source:** Pillar: Flexible — moving off a single-provider platform onto standard, swappable pieces behind ports (ADR-017–022). ### S54 — Budgets in pnpm verify: bundle size, render-count harness, coverage ratchet

**Gap:** ADR-026: at most 200 KB gzipped JavaScript before the page is usable, render-count baselines for heavy views, and coverage floors of 95% (domain) and 85% lines / 80% branches elsewhere. The owner chose to ratchet (2026-10-19): floors go to today's measured values now and every story raises them until the targets are met by the end of the UI band. Measured at HEAD by the reviewers: domain 94.5% lines / 79.5% branches, web 48.5% / 85%, functions 80% / 78%; floors are far lower (web lines 14). No `size-limit`. At `58db7c2` the web build is one entry chunk of 143,833 bytes gzipped (~140 KB), so the 200 KB budget holds with ~60 KB of headroom; `tools/` (S52's lint-rule tests) is not a workspace package and has no coverage floor, so AC 3's "every package" means `packages/*`, `functions` and `web`. **Re-measured at `1967ae3` (2026-10-20 backlog review):** lines / branches / functions / statements: domain 95.95 / 87.5 / 94.28 / 95.95 (already at the 95 target), mlb-api 100 / 88.05 / 100 / 100, functions 80.01 / 78.21 / 87.77 / 80.01, web 47.35 / 84 / 69.81 / 47.35; one entry chunk of 143,827 B gzipped. `packages/ports` is interfaces only: no runtime code, no tests and no coverage block (v8 reports 0% lines for its re-export `index.ts`), so AC 3's floors apply to the packages with runtime code and ports stays without one. **AC 1's 1 KB test cannot read `web/dist`:** `pnpm verify` runs `test:coverage` before `pnpm build`, so on a clean checkout (CI) there is no `dist` yet. The test runs `size-limit` on a temp file instead, under `tools/` like S53's `jscpd` test (picked up by `pnpm test:tools`), and `pnpm verify` runs `size-limit` after `pnpm build`; `tools/` was added to the fence for it. Inserted by the 2026-10-19 design intake review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S54, the app could get heavier and the tests could cover less without anyone noticing. S54 impact: the build fails when the app's code outgrows its size budget or test coverage slips, and slow-to-redraw screens can be measured.

**Source:** Pillar: Dependable — the gates ADR-024–026 require, so duplicated logic, stale comments, slow pages and thin tests are caught by a check rather than by users. Asked whether the guardrail and budget stories may cite Dependable, as S49 does. Approved by owner 2026-10-19: "Yes"

**Depends on:** none.

**Scope files:** `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `web/package.json`, `.size-limit.json`, `web/src/test/`, `tools/`, `web/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/domain/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/ports/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/mlb-api/vitest.config.ts`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `docs/v3/backlog/frame/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

### S77 — Account export and deletion API: download first, then delete everywhere, with maximal verification

**Gap:** ADR-028 (owner, 2026-10-23): a user downloads their data and only then deletes it (*"Yes, but only if download happens before delete"*); deletion is immediate, after maximal verification including a typed phrase (*"Immediately, but with maximal verification including typing a phrase"*); and backups are handled by a deletion log re-applied after any restore. After S76 every store is registered with `exportFor` / `deleteFor`, but no route calls them, nothing checks the confirmation, and nothing records a deletion. The session (S8) is a signed token checked without a database read, so a deleted user's session still verifies until it expires; routes must not treat that as an account.

**Impact:** Before S77, there was no way for a user's data to be downloaded or erased. S77 impact: the server can hand a signed-in user all of their data and then, once they've confirmed every way we can ask, erase it from every place it's kept, at once.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Depends on:** **S76** (the registry and stores), **S8** (session, `IdentityAdmin`), **S44** (route table).

**Scope files:** `packages/domain/`, `packages/ports/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `web/src/api/generated.types.test.ts`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S77.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S77.sh` performs)

1. `GET /api/v1/me/export`, signed in, returns every registered store's `exportFor(uid)` keyed by store name, plus a single-use deletion token bound to that uid that expires within 15 minutes; signed out it is 401 (test).
2. `POST /api/v1/me/delete` with the typed phrase and the deletion token deletes only when all hold, and each refusal is tested: the session was issued within the last 10 minutes (else 403, re-sign-in required); the phrase equals the one exported constant exactly (else 400); the token is valid, unused, unexpired, for this uid and came from an export (else 403, export required).
3. A successful delete runs `deleteFor` on every registered store and `IdentityAdmin.deleteAccount` for each linked identity, then `GET /api/v1/me` with the same session is 401 and no store holds anything for that uid (test). If a store fails, the request fails and a retry finishes the deletion (test with a store that fails once).
4. A deletion log records only the deleted uid and the time, and a `reapplyDeletions` function deletes a uid that a restored backup brought back (test). The deletion log is labeled in S76's classification manifest as the one entry ADR-028 keeps after a deletion (a `retained` label, which a test allows on that entry only); the single-use token record holds no personal field (token ID and expiry only) and is labeled too. (Added by the 2026-10-23 backlog review: S76's manifest fails on an unlabeled class, and `personal` would claim a store deletes the log.)
5. Both routes are in `ApiRoutes`, the spec and the web types (with their `generated.types.test.ts` pairings); `pnpm api:breaking` exits 0.
6. No `console.*` call in code this story adds logs an email or an export body (grep).

(2026-10-24 backlog review: the uid → links read this note also asked for **already exists** since S76: `UserRepository.exportFor(uid)` returns `{ profile, identities: [{ provider, subject }] }` (`packages/ports/src/auth.ts`, `UserDataExport`), and contract case (h) checks it. ### S80 — Separate download from delete: stored downloads that age out in 14 days, twice in 24 hours, linked by email

**Gap:** The owner, 2026-10-27, separated download from delete (ADR-028, replacing 2026-10-23's download-then-delete): *"Deleting and downloading aren't connected. If someone wants to delete their data, they can do it without downloading. If they want to download, they can do it without deleting. If they want to do both, they have to download first, then delete."* Downloads are stored files: *"The download should be hosted in R2 with an expiration (ideally a bucket age-out policy of 14 days). If the account is deleted after that, the data is lost. If not, they can request a new download. They can request a download twice per day."* (rolling 24 hours; a link in Settings and by email: *"Both"*; deleting the account deletes the download: *"Delete them together with a warning shown and a link to the download."*). S77 shipped the opposite: `GET /api/v1/me/export` returns the data inline with a 15-minute single-use deletion token, and `POST /api/v1/me/delete` refuses with 403 `export_required` without one. Nothing stores a download, limits requests, or sends email.

**Impact:** Before S80, someone had to download their data before they could delete their account, and the download existed only in that moment. S80 impact: downloading and deleting are separate choices; a download waits for 14 days, behind a link in Settings and in an email, and goes away with the account.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Depends on:** **S77** (the routes and deletion this changes).

**Scope files:** `packages/domain/`, `packages/ports/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `web/src/api/generated.types.test.ts`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S80.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S80.sh` performs)

1. Requesting a download, signed in, writes every registered store's `exportFor(uid)` (keyed by store name) to an `ExportStore` port in `packages/ports` with an expiry 14 days after it was made, and answers with its id and expiry, not the data; signed out it is 401 (test).
2. A third request inside any rolling 24 hours is refused with 429 and the time the next is allowed; a request 24 hours after the earliest of the two succeeds (test with an injected clock).
3. The user's current download (id and expiry) can be read, and its file fetched by its owner only: another user, an expired download, or none gets 404 (test).
4. A successful request sends one message through a `Mailer` port in `packages/ports` to the account's email, holding a link to BT and no exported data (test against the in-memory mailer).
5. `POST /api/v1/me/delete` deletes with the typed phrase and a recent sign-in alone, with no download made (test); its 403 `reauth_required` and 400 `phrase_mismatch` refusals are kept (test). The deletion token is gone: no `deletionToken`, `DeletionTokenRepository` or `export_required` remains under `packages/` or `functions/src/` (grep).
6. The `ExportStore` is registered in `personalDataStores()` as `Cloud storage: data downloads` and labeled in the classification manifest; deleting an account removes its downloads and request times, and another user's are untouched (test: the store passes the repository contract's deletion case).
7. In-memory `ExportStore` (honouring the 14-day expiry) and `Mailer` adapters live under `functions/src/adapters/memory/` and are what `pnpm dev` uses; no `console.*` call this story adds logs an email address or exported data (grep).
8. The routes are in `ApiRoutes`, the spec and the web types (with their `generated.types.test.ts` pairings); `pnpm api:breaking` exits 0.
9. This file’s S80 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

**Notes (2026-10-27 backlog review, at `63f5e62`):**

- **Where the manifest looks:** `data-classification.test.ts` discovers repository classes only in `functions/src/adapters/memory/repos.ts` (`/^export class (\w+)/gm`). Put `InMemoryExportStore` and `InMemoryMailer` there, or widen that discovery to every file in `adapters/memory/`, which is also inside the fence. Otherwise AC 6 and AC 7 pass with nothing checking their labels.
- **The dev mailer holds addresses.** If `InMemoryMailer` keeps the messages it sends (AC 4's test reads them), each one holds an email address, so it is personal data. A `none` label would be false, and `retained` is only for the deletion log. Its in-memory `deleteFor(uid)` drops that user's messages, so `Mailer.send` carries the uid. When the Cloudflare adapter lands, its own deletion and retention follow that row ("Cloudflare's retention"). If the mailer keeps nothing, label it `none` and say why.
- **Export without nesting:** `ExportStore` is itself a registered store, so its `exportFor(uid)` returns metadata only (ids, expiries, request times), never the stored files. Otherwise each download would contain the one before it.
- **One rule, in `packages/domain` (ADR-025):** the 14-day lifetime and the two-in-rolling-24-hours rule are pure, tested domain functions (for example `downloadExpiresAt` and `nextDownloadAllowedAt(requestTimes, now)`). To carry the next allowed time, add an optional field to `ApiErrorResponse` or give the route its own error type, and add `429` to the route's `ROUTE_DESCRIPTIONS` errors. An optional response field is not breaking.
- **Absolute link:** an email needs BT's full address, and locally the web app (:5173) and API (:8787) are separate. Read an app origin through the existing `SecretsProvider` / environment lookup (`adapters/fixtures/auth.ts`, `local-server.ts`), defaulting to `http://localhost:5173`. - **Rule 21:** run `scripts/verify-S54.sh` before the status flip and raise each floor its check 3 names. At `63f5e62` it is red: functions branches floor 85, measured 86.

### S84 — Graders prove their own story, laws hold forever: pinned re-verification, a laws registry, and every existing grader sorted

**Gap:** A story's grader is meant to prove that story's work, but nothing keeps it to that. Some graders compare the whole repository at HEAD with the state before the story (`git diff <BASE> -- <path>`), so a later story that legitimately changes the same file turns an old grader red: S81 added Playwright to the root `package.json`, and `scripts/verify-S60.sh` check 7 has failed ever since, though S60's own commit (`74a93e0`) never touched that file. `scripts/audit.sh story <ID> --reverify` re-runs a grader against today's tree, and S81's pilot recorded the owner's S60 design verdict through such a re-run, so a design verdict was tied to an unrelated re-check. And there is no list of the requirements that must hold forever: the lines BT already guards in `pnpm verify` (`bt/no-browser-storage`, `bt/no-domain-arithmetic`, the personal-data manifest test, the route-table test, `pnpm size`, the coverage ratchet, rule 22 in `pnpm backlog:check`) are scattered across ADRs and rules. The owner, 2026-10-28, on why S60's grader ran against S83's work: *"Any given story may perform work whose requirements are specific to that story's functionality, but another story might do work that directly conflicts. … We'd only want to check each test's outcomes within the scope of its work, not in the context of the entire system."* and on the model: *"The first would be an "at commit time" check which essentially proves the work is complete as defined at the time it's built, and would only be expected to succeed against the codebase as of the time of its commit. The second would be more of a law, something that defines things which ought to be checked henceforth."* Then: *"I think part of this two-tiered model change needs to be a review of all existing stories' verification passes to sort out any laws from the pinned graders. And lastly, some of the graders were modified after the original commit of the story, and I want to either reverse those changes to match the pattern as if it had existed already OR record something that notes why we did NOT change them despite the updated system."* Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-28.

**Impact:** Before S84, a check written to prove one finished piece of work could start failing months later because a different, perfectly valid change touched the same file, and nothing said which rules must hold forever. S84 impact: each story's proof stays tied to that story's own work, while a short, named list of permanent rules is checked on every change.

**Source:** Feature: Robust core

**Depends on:** **S81** (`scripts/audit.sh --design-match`, which this separates from re-verification).

**Prefer after:** **S83** (the owner put it right after S83, 2026-10-28).

**Scope files:** `scripts/`, `docs/v3/LAWS.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md`, `docs/v3/LOOP.md`

**Scripts exception (owner, 2026-10-28).** Rule 8 keeps every story out of `scripts/` except its own grader. This story exists to change the graders and `scripts/audit.sh`, at the owner's direction (quoted above), so `scripts/` is fenced whole. It does not change product code or any package's tests.

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S84.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S84.sh` performs)

1. The [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract) and backlog rules 7–9 state the two tiers in the owner's words: a **grader** is a commit-time proof of its own story — every "this story didn't change X" check compares the story's own commits (its base to its shipping commit; before the commit, its base to the working tree), never the base to HEAD; a **law** is a check that runs in `pnpm verify` on every commit and is listed in `docs/v3/LAWS.md`; changing or removing a law is an owner decision, recorded like a budget change.
2. `scripts/audit.sh story <ID> --reverify` runs the grader in a temporary git worktree checked out at the story's shipping commit (read from its completion entry in `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`), never at HEAD, and removes the worktree afterwards; a test shows a grader that fails at HEAD but passes at its shipping commit re-verifies as passing.
3. A design-match verdict is recorded on its own — `scripts/audit.sh design <ID> --design-match -` — without running the story's grader; `audit.sh story`'s completion still requires the verdict for a UI story (rule 22). A test shows both.
4. `docs/v3/LAWS.md` lists every law: a short statement, its source (the owner's words, an ADR or a backlog rule), and where it is enforced (the file and the `pnpm verify` step that runs it). Seeded with at least: browser storage only in `web/src/storage/` (`bt/no-browser-storage`), no arithmetic over BT data in views (`bt/no-domain-arithmetic`), every repository labeled in the personal-data manifest, dispatched routes equal `ApiRoutes`, the 200 KB entry budget (`pnpm size`), coverage floors never fall (rule 21), no copy-paste (`pnpm dup:check`), and every UI story carries a design match (rule 22). `pnpm backlog:check` (or a vault test) fails when a listed enforcement file is missing or its step is not in the `verify` chain. A seeded law that `pnpm verify` does not enforce yet is listed as **proposed**, as AC 5 allows (2026-10-28 backlog review: rule 21's "never lower a floor" has no step — `pnpm test:coverage` enforces each floor, nothing checks a floor was not lowered), and the check skips proposed rows.
5. **Every existing grader sorted** (owner: *"a review of all existing stories' verification passes to sort out any laws from the pinned graders"*). A table in `docs/v3/LAWS.md` lists every check of every `scripts/verify-S*.sh` and `scripts/verify-V*.sh` (the vault-migration stages, whose completion entries are in `docs/v3/VAULT-MIGRATION-AUDIT.md`) as **pinned** or **law**. A check classed as a law is either already enforced in `pnpm verify` (named in its row) or listed as **proposed**, with what would enforce it, for a later story — this story adds no product tests. Every pinned check that compares a path with a fixed base at HEAD (`git diff <BASE> -- …`) is rewritten to compare the story's own commits.
6. **Graders edited after their story shipped** (owner: *"either reverse those changes to match the pattern as if it had existed already OR record something that notes why we did NOT change them"*). For each `scripts/verify-S*.sh` and `scripts/verify-V*.sh` with a commit after its story's completion entry, the table records the commit(s) and either restores the grader to what it would have been under the pinned model, or records why it was left as it is. Edits made before the story's completion (its own checkpoints) are not counted.
7. Every grader re-verifies at its shipping commit: `scripts/audit.sh story S60 --reverify` passes all 11 checks (check 7 included) without weakening any, and a run over every `done` story with a completion entry reports each grader's result at its shipping commit (graders that predate the per-check contract report their exit code).
8. `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md` and `docs/v3/LOOP.md` describe a grader as a commit-time proof of its own story and point to `docs/v3/LAWS.md` for the checks that hold forever (owner, 2026-10-28, asked whether S84 should update them: *"Yes, include all three"*) (grep).
9. This file’s S84 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

**Reuse check**

Reuse `scripts/lib/checks.sh`, `scripts/audit.sh`'s entry format and its `BT_AUDIT_*` overrides (S81), the vault tests' throwaway-world pattern (`scripts/backlog-vault/audit-design-match.test.ts`), and the existing guards as they are (register them; don't rewrite them).

**Out of scope**

Writing new enforcement for proposed laws (later stories, one per law), changing product code or package tests, and changing any story's acceptance criteria.

### S87 — The deletion cookie: the server remembers a deleted account once, for its Settings page, and cookies come from one codepath

**Gap:** The owner wants the deletion message shown at `/settings`, *"triggered by visiting the settings page with a server-only cookie that is only sent to users after deletion"* (2026-10-29), shown *"Until seen once"*. A cookie the page's code can't read (`HttpOnly`) has to be set and read by the server: today `POST /api/v1/me/delete` sets no cookie, `GET /api/v1/me` answers a deleted user plain 401, and BT sets no cookies at all. The owner also made the cookie law a conscious choice (asked whether LAWS.md should gain it: *"Yes, add it with S87"*): cookies are set by one codepath only. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-29.

**Impact:** Before S87, nothing could tell a browser that had just deleted its account apart from any signed-out visitor. S87 impact: right after a deletion the server remembers it once, privately, so Settings can show the deletion message on the next visit and then forget it — and any other cookie fails the build until the owner decides otherwise.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Depends on:** **S77** (the delete route).

**Scope files:** `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/domain/`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `web/src/api/generated.types.test.ts`, `docs/v3/LAWS.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S87.sh` performs)

1. A successful `POST /api/v1/me/delete` sets one cookie, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, `Secure` when the request came over HTTPS and not on plain `http://` (owner, 2026-10-29: *"Secure on HTTPS only"* — Safari drops `Secure` cookies on `http://localhost`), with no `Max-Age` or `Expires` (a browser-session cookie), named in one module (`functions/src/services/cookies.ts`); a refused deletion (400, 401, 403) sets none (test).
2. `GET /api/v1/me` with that cookie and no session — no bearer, an invalid one, or one whose account is gone — answers 401 with `error: "account_deleted"`; **any** `/me` response that sees the cookie clears it (`Max-Age=0`), signed in or not, so a second request answers plain 401 (*"Until seen once"*) and a signed-in request still answers 200 while discarding it (owner, 2026-10-29, asked whether a re-sign-in drops the message: *"Drop it (clear on any /me)"*) (test). The spec documents `account_deleted` on `/api/v1/me`'s 401, and the web types are regenerated; `pnpm api:breaking` exits 0.
3. **Law P10, enforced** (owner, 2026-10-29: *"Yes, add it with S87"*): a functions test fails when any API response sets a cookie other than through `cookies.ts` (checked over the route table's responses), and `docs/v3/LAWS.md` lists P10 as enforced with its file and step.
4. The cookie names nothing personal: its value is a fixed marker, not a uid or email (test; ADR-028).

- **The local Node adapter keeps one `Set-Cookie`.** `functions/src/adapters/node/http.ts` writes `Object.fromEntries(response.headers)`, which merges repeated headers. That is fine for the one cookie this story sets or clears per response. If any response ever needs two, use `headers.getSetCookie()` there; the file is inside this fence.

A browser-session cookie fits *"Until seen once"*: closing the browser before visiting only loses a one-time message. A value that identifies the account would need the owner to amend ADR-028 first.

### S79 — Download and delete your data in Settings: stored download link, typed-phrase confirmation, immediate deletion

**Gap:** ADR-028: a signed-in user can download their data and, separately, delete it, immediately, after maximal verification including typing a phrase (owner, 2026-10-23; separated 2026-10-27: *"Deleting and downloading aren't connected."*). S77 and S80 give the server the download and delete routes, with downloads kept 14 days and limited to two in any rolling 24 hours; S78 draws the flow in standings-search-settings A4; S6 builds the Settings page it lives on. The web app has no way to reach any of it, and after a deletion the browser would still hold the session token and cached settings that S76 labeled personal.

**Impact:** Before S79, a user had no button to get their data or erase it. S79 impact: from Settings, a signed-in user can get a download of everything BT holds about them, and can type a phrase to have their account and data erased at once — including what was saved in their browser.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Prefer after:** **S83** (the shell fixes from the owner's comparison of the first shell build), so this story's captures show the corrected shell.

- **How the SPA reaches S87's signal: four things in `web/src/` stand in the way at `aec31e6`, all inside this fence.** (1) `SessionProvider` never calls `GET /api/v1/me` without a stored token (`useState(() => getSessionToken() ? loading : SIGNED_OUT)`), and after deletion `signOut()` drops the token. The cookie is cleared by whichever `/me` arrives first, so if two calls race, the one whose result is used can get a plain 401 and A5 never shows. Ask once per page load, through one shared in-flight promise, only on a signed-out `/settings` (and right after a successful delete, without leaving `/settings`). A plain 401 redirects as before. ### S62 — Load-time budgets and end-to-end flows in CI: Lighthouse CI + Playwright

**Gap:** ADR-026: Largest Contentful Paint < 2.5 s (tiered since 2026-10-29: see the budget change below), Total Blocking Time (the lab stand-in for Interaction to Next Paint) < 200 ms and layout shift < 0.1 on a throttled mid-range phone, median of 3–5 runs, in CI; Playwright flows over the main paths against fixtures. The owner approved Lighthouse CI (2026-10-19, ADR-026) and Playwright in CI (2026-10-19). `ci.yml` runs neither. Placed right after the shell so the budgets guard the UI band while it is built. Inserted by the 2026-10-19 design intake review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Budget change (owner, 2026-10-29):** the Largest Contentful Paint budget is tiered — warn over 2.5 s, block at 5 s (ADR-026 amendment, AC 1). The first real run measured 3.19 s on both pages; "we can figure out the problems later".

**Impact:** Before S62, nobody would learn a page had become slow on a phone until users felt it. S62 impact: every change is timed on a mid-range phone profile and clicked through the main paths. A page slower than the budget gets a warning naming the page and the number; a page that takes 5 seconds or more to show its main content, or that blocks or jumps too much, fails the build.

**Gap:** S84 left two ways to find a story's shipping commit: `story_tip` in `scripts/lib/checks.sh` takes the newest commit whose subject starts `<ID>: `, while `shipping_commit` in `scripts/lib/reverify.sh` reads the ledger (the commit that adds the story's completion entry, or a backfill's `Shipped in`). They already disagree for S7 and S14, V3's ledger commit is a later "V3 done" commit, and the subject rule depends on every checkpoint being worded correctly forever. Asked whether one lookup should replace the other, and accepting the recommendation to use the ledger, the owner answered (2026-10-29): *"Yes"*. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-29.

**Impact:** Before S88, a story's proof could look at a slightly different set of changes depending on which of two lookups ran. S88 impact: every proof finds "the commit this story shipped in" the same way, from the record of what shipped.

### S89 — Faster CI: parallel jobs, flows on several workers, design captures out of pnpm e2e

**Gap:** CI's one `build` job runs `pnpm verify`, the API checks, the Playwright flows and Lighthouse one after another (run 40932706098: verify 1m32s, flows 2m27s before failing). `e2e/playwright.config.ts` pins `workers: 1` because the design captures share one `pnpm dev` server and in-memory data (sign-in, settings, account deletion); `pnpm e2e` runs every spec under `e2e/`, so CI also retakes all the design captures, not only the flows. Asked whether the tests can run on several workers on GitHub, the owner answered (2026-10-29): *"Let's set that aside for now, maybe make a story for it"*. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-29.

**Impact:** Before S89, every push waits for each CI check in turn, and the browser checks also retake every design screenshot. S89 impact: the checks run side by side, so a push learns whether it is green sooner.

**Source:** Pillar: Delightful — faster checks on every change, for performance and customer benefit; the pillar covers developers too. Approved by owner 2026-10-29: "It's more about perf and customer benefit", then, asked whether to cite Delightful or Dependable: "Delightful"

**Depends on:** **S62** (the CI job, `pnpm e2e`, `pnpm lighthouse`).

**Scope files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `lighthouserc.json`, `e2e/`, `package.json`, `scripts/backlog-vault/`, `docs/v3/LAWS.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S89.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** changing CI (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S89.sh` performs)

1. `ci.yml` runs `pnpm verify` (with the API spec checks), the Playwright flows, and Lighthouse as separate jobs that start together; Lighthouse still runs alone on its runner, so nothing else shares the machine it times.
2. `pnpm e2e` runs only `e2e/flows/` (and the harness's own checks), not the design captures; `pnpm design:capture <spec>` still takes them; and CI still runs every `e2e/design/` spec, without `BT_DESIGN_CAPTURE` (so nothing is written to the tree), in its own job beside the others, so a capture spec that breaks still fails CI.
3. The flows run with more than one Playwright worker; each test that signs in or changes data gets its own state, so no flow depends on another's order (a run with `--repeat-each=2` passes).
4. **Lighthouse starts when the app is ready, not after a timeout** (owner, 2026-10-29, asked whether S89 should also fix it: *"Yes"*): in CI, `lhci` no longer logs "Timed out waiting for the server to start listening" — it sees the server's ready line (or `lighthouserc.json` waits on a check that does), so no run waits out `startServerReadyTimeout`.
5. Law P11 still holds: the vault test that reads `ci.yml` finds a step running `pnpm verify`.
6. This file's S89 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

**Notes (2026-10-29 backlog review):**

- **Lighthouse waits a minute for nothing.** The first CI runs logged "Timed out waiting for the server to start listening" from `lhci` and then ran anyway: `lighthouserc.json` waits for `startServerReadyPattern: "Local:"` for up to `startServerReadyTimeout: 60000`. Run locally without a terminal, `pnpm lighthouse:serve` does print `[web]   ➜  Local:   http://localhost:4173/`, so why the runner misses it is not yet known (ANSI codes or buffering are guesses). It costs every CI run up to 60 s and may time pages before `vite preview` is ready. It fits this story's aim, but `lighthouserc.json` is outside the fence, and adding it re-scopes a story whose pillar the owner approved, so it waited for the owner (question raised 2026-10-29). **Answered:** the owner said yes; `lighthouserc.json` is in the fence and AC 4 carries it.

Whatever ready line AC 4 waits on, check it against the server Lighthouse actually starts; moving `lighthouse:serve` onto wrangler is in this fence (`package.json`) if it simplifies AC 4.

### S90 — Next-pitch model: training data, a trained model, and an honest evaluation

**Gap:** BT has every pitch of the games it records (`GameSnapshot.plays`: type, call, count, location, kinematics) but nothing that learns from them. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-29: *"I want to make a story to use pitch data to train a model or a fine tune to predict the next pitch during games"*; asked how, the owner chose *"Train our own small model"* over an LLM fine-tune.

**Impact:** Before S90, BT can only show pitches after they're thrown. S90 impact: BT has a model that, given the game situation, gives the odds of each pitch type and where it's likely to go — and a measured answer to whether it beats simply guessing the pitcher's usual pitch.

**Source:** Feature: Next-pitch prediction

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S90.sh` performs)

1. **An ADR for the model** is proposed in `docs/v3/ARCHITECTURE.md` and accepted by the owner (quoted): where training runs (offline, on a developer machine or CI — never on a request), the training toolchain (inside the locked TypeScript stack, or the case for an exception), the model's file format, and how the Worker evaluates it with no ML runtime of its own (e.g. trees or weights evaluated in plain TypeScript).
2. **Training data** comes from MLB's own pitch-by-pitch recordings via the existing ingest path, never scraped pages: `pnpm pitch-model:collect` records past seasons offline (`BT_USE_LIVE_MLB=1`), folds them with the S63 replay fold, and writes one row per pitch — features known *before* the pitch (pitcher, batter side, count, outs, runners, inning, score margin, the pitcher's previous pitches in the at-bat and his season mix so far) and the label (pitch type, plate location). A small committed sample under `fixtures/pitch-model/` keeps tests offline.
3. **No future leaks into a prediction:** a test shows every feature for pitch *n* is computed from pitches before *n* only, and training / test splits are by date (train on earlier games, test on later ones).
4. **The model** is one named, tested function in `packages/domain` (`predictNextPitch(situation, model) → { types: { type, probability }[]; location: { pX, pZ, spread } }`): pitch-type probabilities sum to 1; the location is a likely spot with its spread.
5. **An honest evaluation** in `scripts/pitch-model/eval.md`, regenerated by `pnpm pitch-model:eval` on the held-out games: log loss and top-1 accuracy for pitch type, and location error, each beside the **baseline** of the pitcher's own pitch mix in that count. The script fails if the model doesn't beat the baseline on pitch type.
6. The model file is small enough to ship to the Worker (target under 1 MB) and `predictNextPitch` runs in under a millisecond per pitch (timed in the test).
7. This file's S90 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

### S103 — Ingest Baseball Savant's per-pitch game feed (what MLB's feeds lack)

**Gap:** Baseball Savant's game feed (`https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/gf?game_pk=823823`; owner, 2026-10-30: *"oh, I forgot, there's also this"*) holds every pitch keyed by the live feed's `playId` (340 of 340 on 823823). Most of it repeats MLB's live feed exactly — the trajectory (`x0`…`az`, spin, breaks, extension, plate time), the strike zone, the box score and season lines — but some is in no MLB feed BT reads: per batted ball expected batting average (`xba`), barrel, spray position in feet and how many ballparks a home run leaves (`homeRunBallparks`); bat speed on every swing; sword swings; Savant's in-zone call; times through the order; the exact ABS-challenged pitch; and the location where the pitch crosses the front of the plate. BT keeps only those (owner, 2026-10-30, asked whether to ingest only what BT doesn't already have: *"Yes re: S103"*). Nothing in the feed says when Savant computed them (owner, 2026-10-30: *"Something that needs to be accounted for is the potential difference in arrival time for the baseball savant details. Since the season is over, I can't tell whether there's any time delta in the realtime arrival of these, unless the data itself tells us something useful."*) — it says only that it is built from MLB's game feed and cached (`"source": "gamefeed"`, `cacheKey`).

**Impact:** Before S103, BT knew how a pitch moved but not what Savant makes of it. S103 impact: each pitch carries Savant's extras — how likely a batted ball was to be a hit, the swing's speed, whether a home run would have left other parks — filling in as Savant publishes them, without ever holding up the live game.

**Source:** Feature: More MLB game data

**Depends on:** **S48** (the per-game ingest object that owns when MLB is called during a game; AC 5 runs inside it).

**Scope files:** `fixtures/`, `packages/mlb-api/src/`, `packages/ports/src/`, `packages/domain/src/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/SAVANT-DATA.md`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

1. `fixtures/raw/savant-gf-823823.json` holds Savant's response to `https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/gf?game_pk={gamePk}` for 823823, recorded once with `BT_USE_LIVE_MLB=1` and committed; tests and local dev read it, never the network.
2. `packages/mlb-api` types the pitch rows as named interfaces and parses them with zod; a parse test runs on the recording, and `pnpm mlb:scan-drift` covers it.
3. `MlbStatsClient` gains `fetchSavantGameFeed(gamePk)`, in the fixture and HTTP adapters (Savant's host as its own base URL); ingest owns the call, no web code fetches it.
4. **Only what MLB's feeds lack.** A mapper projects each pitch, joined by `playId`, into `GameSnapshot.savant` with exactly: `xba`, `isBarrel`, spray `x` / `y` in feet, `homeRunBallparks`, `batSpeed`, `isSword`, `savantInZone`, `timesThroughOrder`, `isAbsChallenge`, and the front-of-plate location (`plateXPoly`, `plateZPoly`); no trajectory, zone, box-score or season field is copied (grep over the mapper), so each value keeps one source (ADR-025). On 823823: 52 batted balls carry `xba`, 150 swings carry `batSpeed`, 2 pitches are swords, and the 5 ABS-challenged pitches are in `atBatIndex` 34, 39, 69, 82, 83 (Savant's `ab_number` is one higher) (tests). Additive to the payload (`pnpm api:breaking` exits 0).
5. **Arrival time is accounted for** (owner, 2026-10-30, quoted in the Gap):
   - Savant is pulled on its own cadence inside S48's ingest object, never in the same call as the live feed, so a slow or failing Savant never delays a pitch (test with a hanging Savant fake);
   - each Savant field is empty until it arrives and is merged into its pitch by `playId` as it does, a newer value replacing an older one only by version (ADR-022), and views read an absent field as "not yet", never as zero (unit tests on the merge);
   - for each pitch BT records when each Savant field first appeared beside the live feed's time for that pitch (`playEndTime`), so the real delay can be read once live games resume (test on a two-poll sequence);
   - polling is bounded: at most every N seconds while the game is in its live window (N in config) and once more after the final for late fields (test).
6. The source is optional: when Savant fails or returns nothing, `savant` is absent and the game is served as before (test).
7. **Terms of use first** (owner, 2026-10-30, asked whether one story should check Savant's terms of use before any live Savant call ships, covering the data, the field drawings and query-engine use, as a requirement on the first Savant story: *"Sure"*). ### S104 — Ingest pitcher season averages from Baseball Savant

**Gap:** BT knows each pitch's speed, spin and break but not what is normal for the pitcher, so it can't say "1.5 mph above his average". Savant's `pitcher-yearly-averages` feed gives each pitcher's season averages per pitch type, for any list of pitchers in one call (owner, 2026-10-30, asked whether the two game-context Savant feeds should join "More MLB game data" as stories: *"1. Yes"*). What it holds: `docs/v3/SAVANT-DATA.md`.

**Impact:** Before S104, BT could show how a pitch moved but not whether that was usual for the pitcher. S104 impact: BT keeps every pitcher's season norms per pitch type for the games it follows, ready for the Live and Plays rooms to compare each pitch with.

**Source:** Feature: More MLB game data

**Depends on:** **S103** (the first Savant story: its AC 7 checks Savant's terms of use before any live Savant call ships, and it sets up Savant's host in the HTTP adapter).

**Scope files:** `fixtures/`, `packages/mlb-api/src/`, `packages/ports/src/`, `packages/domain/src/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S104.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** building (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S104.sh` performs)

1. `fixtures/raw/savant-pitcher-averages-823823.json` holds Savant's response to `https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/gamefeed/pitcher-yearly-averages?pitchers=[{ids}]` for the pitchers who pitched in 823823 (from the live feed), recorded once with `BT_USE_LIVE_MLB=1` and committed; tests and local dev read it, never the network.
2. `packages/mlb-api` types a pitcher row as named interfaces and parses it with zod. The fields are per pitch type, with a prefix (`ff_avg_speed`, `sl_avg_spin`, …), so the parser reads every pitch-type prefix the recording has, not a hand-written list per pitch. A parse test runs on the recording, and `pnpm mlb:scan-drift` covers it.
3. `MlbStatsClient` gains `fetchPitcherSeasonAverages(pitcherIds)`, in the fixture and HTTP adapters. Ingest owns the call (ADR-002), and no web code fetches it.
4. A mapper projects it into BT's own shape, `GameSnapshot.pitcherAverages`, keyed by pitcher id and then by MLB's pitch-type code. Each entry holds usage (count and share), the average and range of speed, spin, horizontal break, vertical and induced vertical break, spin axis, and release point x / y / z, plus the season it covers. A pitcher Savant returns no row for is absent, never zero (tests on the recording). Additive to the payload (`pnpm api:breaking` exits 0).
5. **Cadence:** fetched once for the starting pitchers when the game enters its live window, and once for each reliever the first time he appears; never once per pitch (test with a counting fake over the 823823 replay: as many calls as distinct pitchers entering, at most).
6. The source is optional: when Savant fails or returns nothing, `pitcherAverages` is absent and the game is served as before (test).

**Gap:** Nothing deploys Baseball Theater. A GitHub Actions workflow builds and runs `pnpm verify`, then deploys a preview Worker per pull request against the staging database (never production): previews and staging bind the same `bt-staging` Hyperdrive config on the Neon `staging` branch, which the workflow creates when it's missing (AC 5) (owner, 2026-11-05: "Previews share staging db"), and posts its address (workflow file; a dry run with `wrangler deploy --dry-run` in CI).

4. Secrets (Cloudflare API token, Neon credentials) come from GitHub secrets, never the repo (grep).
5. Every deploy (preview, staging, production) runs `pnpm db:migrate` against its own database before the new Worker takes traffic, then `pnpm db:reapply-deletions` (S113), so a restored database never brings a deleted account back without anyone remembering a runbook step. Each environment's Hyperdrive config is found by its constant name (`bt-production`, `bt-staging`) and created only when missing, with its id resolved at deploy time rather than pasted into `wrangler.jsonc`, so production and staging share one code path. ### S115 — Design captures on request in GitHub Actions

**Gap:** A UI story's design match (rule 22) needs `pnpm design:capture <ID>`, which starts the app as `pnpm dev` does (Postgres in Docker) and drives a browser. ### S116 — Sign in with Logto (email one-time code) on the deployed sites

**Gap:** The only sign-in BT has is the local dev stand-in (`Bearer dev:<uid>`), and S114 AC 7 turns it off on every deployed site, so nobody can sign in on staging or production. ADR-019 chose Logto Cloud for sign-in (email, passwordless, no passkeys at launch) behind the identity ports that already exist: `IdentityProvider.completeSignIn` takes a Logto ID token, `IdentityAdmin` lists, disables and deletes accounts, and the web `Session.signIn()` is the one entry point the header's "Sign in" calls (`web/src/session/session.ts`). No adapter implements them for Logto yet. Inserted by the owner, 2026-11-05 (asked whether a Logto story should be sliced to land before the production release: *"Yes it is ok re: logto, and add a logto story ahead of production"*).

**Impact:** Before S116, the deployed Baseball Theater had no way to sign in, so settings and account features only worked on a developer's machine. S116 impact: fans sign in on the real site with a one-time code sent to their email, and Baseball Theater can launch with accounts.

**Source:** Feature: Modern membership

**Depends on:** **S114** (the deployed environments, their `vars` and Worker secrets, and AC 7's rule that the dev sign-in exists only locally). The first production release waits for this story (owner, 2026-11-05); since the branch flow of 2026-11-06 that release is the owner's first merge of `stage` into `main`, with no approval step.

**Scope files:** `.github/workflows/`, `functions/`, `web/`, `packages/domain/src/`, `packages/domain/vitest.config.ts`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `README.md`, `openapi/bt-api.v1.json`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

0. Write `scripts/verify-S116.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S116.sh` performs)

1. A Logto `IdentityProvider` adapter under `functions/src/adapters/` completes a sign-in from a Logto ID token as the port describes: it checks the signature against the tenant's JWKS (`<endpoint>/oidc/jwks`), that the issuer is `<endpoint>/oidc`, that the audience is the web app's ID and that the token hasn't expired, and returns `{ provider: "logto", subject: sub, email, emailVerified: email_verified }`. It refuses a bad signature, issuer, audience, an expired token, and a token without an email (tests sign tokens with a locally made key and serve its JWKS from a fetch stand-in; no network).
2. The Worker offers the Logto provider in every environment whose `vars` name `LOGTO_ENDPOINT` and `LOGTO_APP_ID`, and the dev provider only where S114 AC 7 allows it: a valid Logto ID token signs in through a sign-in route this story adds to the API route table (so `openapi/bt-api.v1.json` lists it, regenerated by `pnpm api:spec`), which calls the provider's `completeSignIn` and the existing `signIn` and returns BT's own session token, and a `dev:` token is refused (workerd test). (Corrected by the 2026-11-05 backlog review: HEAD has no sign-in route; the dev sign-in signs in on every request through `authenticate`, `functions/src/services/accounts.ts:107`.)
3. The web app's `AuthClient` (ADR-019) is the only module that imports Logto's browser SDK (grep). On a deployed site `Session.signIn()` sends the user to Logto's hosted sign-in with the `email` scope, a callback route finishes it and hands the ID token to BT once, and `signOut()` ends both BT's session and Logto's; locally the dev sign-in is unchanged (RTL tests with a stand-in client). Every `signIn()` asks Logto for a fresh sign-in (`prompt=login`), so Settings' "Sign in again" before deleting an account sends a new emailed code, as ADR-028's recent-sign-in check requires, rather than coming back on Logto's own session (RTL test: the stand-in client is asked with `prompt: "login"`). Every browser key Logto's SDK writes goes through `web/src/storage/` (labeled personal in `STORAGE_KEYS`) and is gone after `signOut()` and after account deletion; `bt/no-browser-storage` is not disabled anywhere (RTL test reads `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` after sign-out; grep). (Added by the 2026-11-05 backlog review.)
4. A Logto `IdentityAdmin` adapter lists, disables (`PATCH /api/users/{id}/is-suspended`) and deletes (`DELETE /api/users/{id}`) accounts through the Management API, with machine-to-machine credentials from Worker secrets; account deletion (S77) deletes a user's Logto account through it (tests with a fetch stand-in). Only production has the machine-to-machine app (owner, 2026-11-06/07, asked whether the Logto plan includes one machine-to-machine app at no extra cost and the $8 is only for a second: "Yes"), so its secret is a production Worker secret only, and the Worker composes the Logto admin only where that secret is set; staging has no Logto admin, and deleting an account there still succeeds and removes staging's rows (test).
5. The Logto endpoint and app ID are `vars` per environment in `wrangler.jsonc`; the machine-to-machine secret is a Worker secret pushed from GitHub secrets on every production deploy (S114 AC 8), never the repo (grep). Staging never uses production's Logto tenant: it signs in through a separate staging Logto tenant or a fake identity shim (owner, 2026-11-06: "We will use a staging one or a fake shim"), so staging's accounts are test accounts and the staging branch never holds a fan's data (S114 AC 9). Previews offer no Logto sign-in (owner, 2026-11-06/07, asked "Are you okay with PR previews not having sign-in, so staging is where you test it?": "Yes", superseding 2026-11-05's "Yes to Logto" for previews): `env.preview` names no Logto vars, and the `preview` and `preview-teardown` jobs read no Logto value (grep and workflow check). Production's tenant endpoint, app ID and machine-to-machine secret appear only in `env.production` and the `production` job, and the `staging` job reads only staging's vars and no machine-to-machine secret (grep and workflow check). (Added applying the owner's answer to the 2026-11-06 backlog review; narrowed by the owner's answers of 2026-11-06/07.) Every production deploy sets production's web app redirect and sign-out URIs through the Management API from constants in the repo (and the email one-time-code sign-in settings, if the API exposes them), idempotently, so no production address is entered in Logto's console by hand (owner, 2026-11-05: "Agreed on all points"; workflow check: only the `production` job runs it, and a test with a fetch stand-in runs it twice). `README.md` documents the owner's Logto setup that stays manual: the production tenant at `auth.baseball.theater` and the staging tenant (or, if the shim is used, that staging has no tenant), each one's single-page app, email sign-in with a one-time code (and a link in the same email if Logto offers it), production's one machine-to-machine app with Management API access, and, because staging has no machine-to-machine app, staging's redirect and sign-out URIs entered once by hand in its console. Any step a workflow performs is idempotent (owner, 2026-11-05: "All the bootstrapping should be like that").
