### S47 — Graduated edge caching + refresh-on-read

**Gap:** ADR-021 applies the cache-lifetime ladder twice — the edge `s-maxage` and the MLB refresh-on-read — with `stale-while-revalidate`. At HEAD handlers send no `Cache-Control` and `functions/src/services/refresh.ts` uses a fixed `CACHE_TTL_MS`. `scripts/verify-S17.sh` check 1 greps `export const CACHE_TTL_MS`, so it stays as the documented floor. Inserted by the 2026-10-18 backlog review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S47, every finished game was re-fetched from MLB every few minutes for as long as anyone looked at it. S47 impact: the longer a game goes unchanged, the longer Cloudflare serves it straight from its cache, so finished games stop costing MLB calls and database reads within hours — while a correction still shows up within two days at most.

**Source:** Feature: Daily scoreboard by date; Game → Live play / linescore context

**Depends on:** **S43** (`cacheLifetimeMs`), **S45** (Worker responses), **S46** (`lastChangedAt`).

**Scope files:** `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `README.md`, `docs/v3/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Parked for the owner (2026-10-30 backlog review, after S45):** on Cloudflare a Worker runs *in front of* the cache, so a `Cache-Control: s-maxage` header on a response the Worker builds is not stored at the edge by itself (Cloudflare docs, "How the cache works": *"Cloudflare Workers run before the cache"*). Two ways to get ADR-021's edge cache, and they differ in cost and behavior:

- **Workers Cache:** `"cache": { "enabled": true }` in `wrangler.jsonc` (wrangler 4.149.0's schema has it). Cloudflare then checks the cache before running the Worker, honors `Cache-Control` per RFC 9111 (`stale-while-revalidate` included), and is *"tiered by default"*, as ADR-021 asks. But *"when caching is enabled, every request to your Worker is charged at the standard Workers request rate … including requests that are normally free: static asset requests"*, which changes ADR-017's cost line.
- **Cache API** (`caches.default.match` / `put` in the Worker): no billing change, but *"The Cache API is not compatible with tiered caching"* (one data center at a time), and the Worker still runs on every request.

**Answered (owner, 2026-10-30): "Workers cache".** The edge cache is Workers Cache, so ADR-021's tiered edge cache holds as written and ADR-017's cost line now includes every request at the Workers rate (static assets too); recording that in ADR-017 is left to the next backlog review, outside this fence. ### S48 — Per-game ingest Durable Object + cron ensure-running

**Gap:** ADR-020 layer 1: a cron wakes one `game-ingest:<gamePk>` Durable Object per in-window game; its alarm polls MLB, writes Postgres, **then** publishes to the game's registered hubs, with hub leases kept in its storage. At HEAD S16's `tickIngest` runs on `setInterval` in `local-server.ts`, and the baseline says "Not yet a deployed scheduled function". Inserted by the 2026-10-18 backlog review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged). The 2026-10-20 backlog review's duplication sweep found `functions/src/services/ingest.ts:70` deciding "final" inline (`codedGameState !== "F"`), which disagrees with `isFinalStatus` (`F`, `O`, `C`): a game-over game outside the window is never fetched. S48 rewrites that per-game decision, so AC 8 makes it one implementation.

**Impact:** Before S48, live games were only polled while a developer's laptop server was running. S48 impact: each live game gets its own always-recovering poller that saves every change before telling anyone about it.

**Source:** Feature: Daily scoreboard by date; Game → Live play / linescore context

### S18 — Live hub Durable Object + LiveGameHub port + one-way WebSocket

**Gap:** ADR-020 layer 2 and ADR-022: per game, hub object(s) `game-hub:<gamePk>:<region>` hold viewers' hibernated, one-way WebSockets and broadcast what the ingest object (S48) publishes — only newer versions, full state on connect when the viewer is behind (`?since=`), loaded from the repository after a cold start, registered with ingest by lease. WebSockets exist only for in-window games. Re-scoped by the 2026-10-18 backlog review to the accepted ADRs; the prior text is in git history.

**Impact:** Before S18, there was no way for the app to tell a browser "this game you're watching just changed". S18 impact: the backend pushes each saved change to everyone watching that game, recovers on its own after a restart, and never sends a viewer the same update twice.

### S19 — Web client auto-updates watched game

**Gap:** Game page is one-shot fetch; Live/Plays/etc. do not move when BT updates. ADR-020's client layer and ADR-022 add: WebSocket only, apply only newer versions, reconnect with backoff and `?since=`, refetch on a version gap, fall back to short-polling, reconnect on tab-visible / online. Re-scoped by the 2026-10-18 backlog review to the accepted ADRs; the prior text is in git history.

**Impact:** Before S19, opening a game page fetched it once and then never changed, even if the score moved. S19 impact: a game page you're watching updates itself live, catches up on its own after a dropped connection, and never jumps backward.

### S28 — Version sunset path: deprecation headers + stale-client upgrade

**Gap:** [ADR-015](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-015--api-versioning--compatibility-accepted) makes additive-only the thing that protects a stale client *while a version lives*. Nothing covers the moment a version is **retired**: no `Deprecation` / `Sunset` signaling, no per-version usage logging to make retirement evidence-based, and no client path for "the version you were built against is gone." [FEATURES](./FEATURES.md) carries *Update / change log UX* as the product surface for exactly this.

**Impact:** Before S28, there was no plan for what happens to someone still running an old version of the app once that version is retired — it would just start failing with no explanation. S28 impact: an outdated app tells the person using it that an update is available, instead of silently breaking, and what's already on their screen stays readable while they update.

**Re-scoped by the 2026-10-19 design intake review:** ADR-023 makes the PWA's update notice "where S28's stale-client upgrade lands": the 426 prompt uses the same `NoticeSlot` / `NoticeBanner` as the service-worker update (S60, S73), so there is one notice component.

**Source:** Feature: Update / change log UX

**Design:** S31 — build to the approved frames in `docs/v3/visual/shell-scoreboard/`. This story may only move to `doing` once every design story named here is `done` (rule 18; `pnpm backlog:check` enforces it).

**Why here:** Last of the versioning work, and the only part that is not needed until there is a real deployed client to be stale. It must land **before the first public deploy** (Later theme: Cloudflare deploy) — until then nothing can be skewed.

**Contract gates (2026-10-14 backlog review).** A `426` response with the `version_unsupported` error body (AC 3) is a handler error response, which the S27 spec declares per route, changes the API contract, so the committed spec `openapi/bt-api.v1.json` must be regenerated (`pnpm api:spec`; `functions/src/services/openapi.test.ts` fails on a stale copy) along with `web/src/api/generated/bt-api.v1.ts` (`web/src/api/codegen.test.ts`). `openapi/` was outside this fence, which would have been a rule-10 stop at the first `pnpm verify`; it is now inside. The ratified prompt is S31's `notice-banner` in the app-level notice slot directly under the header, at every pairing, with a Primary `Reload` action and a dismiss `✕` (`docs/v3/visual/shell-scoreboard/DESIGN.md`, "Work required" → S28).

**Depends on:** S26 (versioned routes), S25 (one ingress helper to put the check in). Also **S73** (the floating update notice A6 makes one component; added by the 2026-11-02 design intake review — `api/versionNotice.ts` already imports S73's `UPDATE_MESSAGE`). Also **S81** (design capture harness, rule 22).

**Scope files:** `packages/domain/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/`, `web/vitest.config.ts`, `README.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `e2e/design/`, `docs/v3/design-checks/`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S28.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S28.sh` performs)

1. Version lifecycle state lives in **one** exported place (e.g. `supported` / `deprecated` / `sunset` per version, with the sunset date), in `packages/domain/` alongside the S26 route table.
2. A functions test: a request to a version marked `deprecated` returns **200** plus `Deprecation` and `Sunset` response headers (RFC-style), and the body is unchanged. Exits 0 in isolation.
3. A functions test: a request to a version marked `sunset` returns **426** with a JSON error code exactly `version_unsupported`, and does **not** return payload data. Exits 0 in isolation.
4. Per-version observability: the handler records the requested version on each API request through a logger or counter seam that a test can assert (the test asserts two different versions produce two distinct records). No external telemetry service.
5. Client handling: the single S25/S26 ingress helper detects **426** and surfaces an app-level "reload to update" state. A web test asserts a mocked 426 produces that affordance and that it is **not** rendered on a normal 200. Exits 0 via `pnpm --filter @bt/web exec vitest run` on that file alone.
6. The 426 path does **not** clear or corrupt already-loaded cache data (a stale screen stays readable behind the prompt — [VISUAL-DESIGN D7](./VISUAL-DESIGN.md#1-design-goals) respect-attention). The web test asserts previously rendered content is still present.
7. `README.md` documents the lifecycle states, that retirement requires the usage log to show no traffic, and that `pnpm verify` never needs network for any of it.
8. The 426 prompt renders through the shared `NoticeSlot` / `NoticeBanner` (S60); no second notice component exists (grep).
9. Design match (rule 22): for each ratified frame this story builds (every state and pairing its ACs name; desktop captured at 1200px, owner 2026-10-28: *"Capture at 1200px"*), `pnpm design:capture S28` (S81) saves the built page in that state and pairing to `docs/v3/design-checks/S28/<frame>.png` from `e2e/design/S28.spec.ts`; the grader checks each file exists at its pairing's width. Regions a later story builds are listed in the spec as expected differences and not judged (owner, 2026-10-28: *"Judge only the story's own parts"*). The story parks `blocked` with its captures committed until the owner says each pair matches, recorded with `scripts/audit.sh story S28 --design-match -`.
10. This file's S28 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

**Out of scope**

- Choosing the actual sunset window length (ADR-015 "Still open" — needs a real deploy first).
- The full changelog/"what's new" content surface; this story ships the *upgrade prompt*, not release notes.
- Service-worker update detection itself — S73.
- Creating a v2 to test against. Version lifecycle state is data; tests drive it with fixtures.

**Needs human judgment**

- Whether the reload prompt's wording and placement are right (the script only checks it appears on 426 and not on 200).
- Whether 426 is preferable to 410 for a retired version. ADR-015 picks 426 because the client action is "upgrade," not "this resource is gone."

**Goal condition:** scripts/verify-S28.sh exits 0, pnpm verify exits 0, no files outside packages/domain/, functions/src/, functions/vitest.config.ts, openapi/, web/src/, web/vitest.config.ts, README.md, docs/v3/BACKLOG.md, docs/v3/backlog/, docs/v3/AUDIT.md, CHANGELOG.md, e2e/design/, docs/v3/design-checks/ are modified, no files under scripts/ or test/ are modified, or stop after 18 turns. If a criterion cannot be met inside that path list, stop and report which criterion and which path — do not widen the scope yourself.

**Notes (2026-11-02 backlog review):**

- **AC 4's record is a log line (ADR-028: "Server and email logs: must not carry personal fields").** It carries the requested version and the route only: no uid, session token, email or IP. The logger stays a port the test can read; nothing is stored.
- **The ingress helper is the `openapi-fetch` client's middleware** (`web/src/api/client.ts`: `api.use({ onRequest })`, S59). The 426 check is an `onResponse` on that same client, not a wrapper around each `fetch*` call (AC 5).

**Notes (2026-11-02 design intake review, A6):** the design-match verdict is shell-scoreboard A6, which replaces the "Contract gates" paragraph's description of the prompt (slot under the header, `Reload`, ✕).

- Reuse S73's floating notice and its one snooze key; build nothing new. AC 8 is met by `NoticeBanner` in `NoticeSlot.tsx`; keep the words "426", "200" and "readable" in test titles (checks 5 / 6) and re-take `shell-notice-*`.
- **Update Now after a 426 must not only call `window.location.reload()`.** With `registerType: "prompt"` and `navigateFallback: "/index.html"` (`web/src/pwa/options.ts`), a plain reload is answered from the old precached shell, which gets 426 again and loops. Ask the worker for the new version (`registration.update()`), activate it, then reload (test).
- **One "keep what's on screen" rule (ADR-025).** `ScoreboardPage.tsx` (`error && !day`) and `StandingsPage.tsx` (`error && !standings`) repeat it, and `GamePage.tsx` (`if (error)`) breaks it: a 426 on a game refetch swaps the room for the error screen. Make it one rule all three use (e.g. a helper that shows `ViewState` error only with no data).
- Turn cap 16 → 18.

**Turn cap:** 16 (+2 for the rule 22 design match, 2026-10-28 design intake; was 14) — assumes lifecycle state as data, header + 426 behavior in the existing handler, one logging seam, and one client prompt wired into the single ingress helper. If it turns into a general notifications/release-notes feature, stop: that is the FEATURES *Update / change log UX* theme, not this story.

A draft design no longer makes a design intake review due (`scripts/review-debt.sh`).
- 2026-11-09 — **S124** done: `GET /api/v1/schedule/month/:month` (`YYYY-MM`, 1901-04 on, checked by `isCalendarMonth` in `packages/domain/src/calendar-date.ts`; after December of next year, by MLB's today, a 400 `month_too_late` from `latestScheduleMonth`, owner 2026-11-09: "Reject past next year") answers every day of a month with its number of games, counted from the stored schedule days (`monthGameCounts`) in one query (`ScheduleRepository.listGameCounts`, `jsonb_array_length` in Postgres), never from the games table. Days of the current season through next year (`scheduleFillWindow`) that BT lacks, or whose month has outlived its ADR-021 lifetime, are asked of MLB with one schedule-only range request (`MlbStatsClient.fetchScheduleRange`, `startDate`/`endDate`; on the HTTP, fixture and overlay clients) and stored through `storeSchedule`, with no game hydrated; a day still unknown is `count: null`, distinct from `0`. The response is cached by when the month last changed (`edgeCacheControl`). The web client has `fetchScheduleMonth` for **S125**'s calendar.
- 2026-11-08 — **S117** done: `pnpm db:copy-baseball` copies production's baseball data (the tables `DATA_CLASSIFICATION` labels `none`: `schedule_days`, `games`, `game_projections`, `replay_artifacts`) into staging or any target, never a personal table or the deletion log; it only adds (no delete, truncate or drop; matching columns only; version-guarded upserts keep newer target rows), migrates the target first, reads production only in read-only transactions (safe through a pooler), and refuses production by name (`production`, `bt-production`), Neon default branch or host (S122's `checkBackfillTarget`, no override). It runs only by hand: the `workflow_dispatch`-only `.github/workflows/copy-baseball-data.yml` (`--neon staging`, on `stage`); no deploy runs it. Not yet run for real: staging's deploy was failing Neon authentication (HTTP 401) on 2026-11-08, which must be fixed first.
- 2026-11-08 — **S122** done: `pnpm mlb:backfill [--from] [--to]` hydrates every game between two dates (default a year back to MLB's today; never before 1901-04-18; November 15 – February 15 skipped by `isOffSeasonDay`) newest first into the local Postgres or `BT_DATABASE_URL`, refusing production without `--allow-production`; days and final games go through ingest's version-guarded `storeSchedule` / `ingestGame`, a complete day asks MLB nothing, a projection left behind its snapshot is repaired, `PoliteFetch` keeps 2 requests in flight per host with 1 s / 3 s gaps and backoff on 429/5xx, each extra source is given up after 14 failed days of games (streaks in `.backfill/<host>--<db>.json`), and the run ends with each game table's rows and `pg_total_relation_size`. The full run back to 1901 is the owner's, on his Mac.
